name: Babysit a pull request
description: Watch one pull request until it is green and clean: poll CI and review feedback, hand each round of failures to a harness that fixes them at the root and pushes, and stop when nothing actionable is left or the round cap is hit.

inputs.name: pr
inputs.description: Pull request number or URL to babysit.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: owner/name to target. Empty means the checkout's own remote.

inputs.name: cwd
inputs.description: Checkout to run gh and the fixing harness in, relative to the workspace.

inputs.name: feedback_command
inputs.description: Optional command collecting review feedback. It must print JSON carrying `unresolvedThreads` and `changesRequested` counts, and it can read $PR and $REPO from the environment — e.g. `pr-comments "$PR" --json -R "$REPO"`. It runs through `$SHELL -l`, so it is written in the operator's own login shell and sees their PATH and helper scripts; the rest of the step stays POSIX. Empty falls back to `gh pr view`, which sees review verdicts but not thread resolution state.

args.script:
set -u
repo_arg=""
[ -n "${REPO:-}" ] && repo_arg="--repo ${REPO}"

# Reading the pull request is the one thing this step cannot fail quietly at:
# a missing `gh`, a stale token, or the wrong repo would otherwise yield an
# empty document that `assess` reads as "nothing to do" and reports green. So
# this one is fatal, and says which pull request it could not read.
if ! pr=$(gh pr view "$PR" $repo_arg --json number,title,url,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,headRefName 2>&1); then
  printf 'cannot read pull request %s: %s\n' "$PR" "$pr" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# `gh pr checks` exits non-zero when checks are failing or pending, which is
# exactly the case this node exists to report — so its status cannot be the
# signal here. Nor can it separate "checks failed" from "the API refused":
# both are exit 1. The *shape* of the output can, and it is the only thing
# that distinguishes real data from an error, so that is what decides.
#
# `bucket` is what collapses GitHub's dozen states into
# pass/fail/pending/skipping/cancel; classifying on raw `state` misses
# ACTION_REQUIRED and EXPECTED, which block a merge while looking like
# neither a failure nor a pending run.
checks=$(gh pr checks "$PR" $repo_arg --json name,state,bucket,link 2>&1 || true)
case "$checks" in
  # A JSON array is data, whatever the exit code said.
  \[*) ;;
  # A PR with no CI at all is a real answer, not a failure.
  *"no checks reported"*) checks='[]' ;;
  # Anything else — an auth failure, a gh too old for `bucket`, a network
  # error — must not read as "no checks", which settles the run green
  # without ever having seen the check suite.
  *)
    printf 'cannot read check status for %s: %s\n' "$PR" "$checks" >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

if [ -n "${FEEDBACK_COMMAND:-}" ]; then
  # Only the operator's own command crosses into the operator's own shell.
  # This script body is POSIX and stays on the step's POSIX shell: running the
  # whole thing under `$SHELL` would break outright for anyone whose login
  # shell is fish, which is precisely the user this option exists to serve.
  # `-l` sources their startup files, so their PATH and helper scripts
  # (`pr-comments` and friends) are on hand for that one call.
  if ! feedback=$("${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -l -c "$FEEDBACK_COMMAND" 2>&1); then
    printf 'feedback_command failed: %s\n' "$feedback" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # An empty result is a failed lookup too, not "no feedback": the fallback
  # below would turn it into {}, zero blocking feedback, and a green report for
  # a source that was never read.
  if [ -z "$feedback" ]; then
    printf 'feedback_command printed nothing; it must print JSON carrying unresolvedThreads and changesRequested\n' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Exiting 0 with the wrong shape is the remaining way to look like "no
  # feedback": a helper that caught its own lookup failure and printed {} or an
  # error object would have both counters default to zero downstream. A
  # substring check rather than a parse, to keep this step free of a jq
  # dependency — it is a schema smoke test, not a validator.
  for required in '"unresolvedThreads"' '"changesRequested"'; do
    case "$feedback" in
      *"$required"*) ;;
      *)
        printf 'feedback_command output is missing %s: %s\n' "$required" "$feedback" >&2
        exit 1 ;;
    esac
  done
else
  # The default source, and fatal for the same reason the others are: an
  # auth or API error here after the PR read succeeded would zero
  # changesRequested, and a PR with requested changes would report green.
  # `unresolvedThreads` is 0 rather than a count because this path cannot see
  # thread resolution state at all — that is what feedback_command is for.
  if ! feedback=$(gh pr view "$PR" $repo_arg --json reviewDecision,reviews,comments -q '{unresolvedThreads: 0, changesRequested: (if .reviewDecision == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" then 1 else 0 end), detail: .}' 2>&1); then
    printf 'cannot read review state for %s: %s\n' "$PR" "$feedback" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Both branches guarantee a JSON object by here, so anything else means a
# lookup reported success while producing something unusable.
case "$feedback" in
  \{*) ;;
  *)
    printf 'review feedback for %s is not a JSON object: %s\n' "$PR" "$feedback" >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

printf '{"checks":%s,"pr":%s,"feedback":%s}\n' "$checks" "$pr" "$feedback"

set.actionable: =([.item.json.output.checks[]? | select(.bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "cancel")] | length) > 0 or ((.item.json.output.feedback.unresolvedThreads // 0) + (.item.json.output.feedback.changesRequested // 0)) > 0 or (.item.json.output.pr.mergeable == "CONFLICTING") or (.item.json.output.pr.mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY")

config.prompt:
="Work in the checkout at " + .inputs.cwd + ", which is the one the pull request was read from — an agent step starts at the workspace root, not there.

Pull request " + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.url // ("#" + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.number | tostring))) + " on branch " + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.headRefName // "?") + " is not ready.

Failing checks:
" + (.nodes.assess.item.failing | tostring) + "

Review feedback:
" + (.nodes.assess.item.feedback | tostring) + "

Merge state: " + ((.nodes.assess.item.pr.mergeStateStatus // "UNKNOWN") | tostring) + (if .nodes.assess.item.conflicted then " — this branch conflicts with its base; merge the base in and resolve every conflict by understanding what both sides changed, never by taking one side wholesale." else "" end) + "

This is round " + (.nodes.watch.iteration | tostring) + " of 8. Check out that branch, fix every failure at its root, and push. Never skip hooks, never disable or weaken a test, and never force a check green. Reply to and resolve each review thread you address, and say plainly which ones you are declining and why."

args.script:
set -u
# Nothing is actionable. If checks are still running, sleeping before the
# next poll is the whole point of the round; if none are, this settles.
if [ "${PENDING:-0}" != "0" ]; then sleep 60; fi
printf '{"settled":%s}\n' "$([ "${PENDING:-0}" = "0" ] && echo true || echo false)"
